entries.text: The party accepted Ashliel's shelter at the roofless chapel, where Sali, a translucent slime-girl, emerged from the trees and begged to join them. Despite Ashliel's pleas to turn back, Max Nightriver led the group north past the shrine stones into a valley, where the Lady of the Forest confronted them before a glowing city.
entries.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: The figure's presence is like a chord of music held just on the edge of hearing, a pressure in the air that makes breath catch in throats. She doesn't move, doesn't speak, simply watches as the party descends the slope.
Sali stops just before the light of the city touches her feet, her excitement finally seeming to dampen into something closer to awe. She looks back at the party, then at the silver-haired woman, then back again. "That's her," she whispers, her voice trembling. "The Lady. I've... I've dreamed of this place."
The Lady of the Forest finally speaks, and her voice carries through the valley without her shouting, clear as a bell. "Travelers. You have come far, and crossed many lines." Her gaze fixes on Max Nightriver with an intensity that feels like weight on the chest. "Tell me: do you come seeking something lost, or do you come to take something that was never yours?"
Adolion Narrator: Ten steps past the shrine stones every bird stops singing. Between two trunks stands a stag, perfectly still, and when it opens its mouth there is a second pair of eyes inside, looking out.

arcs.text: Ashliel asks the party to turn back in the morning, but the checkpoint goal is to go north into the elves' wood — the party must decide whether to heed her or press on.
Sali asks to join the party as an adventurer — the party must decide whether to take her along.
Something pale green is watching the party from beyond the chapel's broken wall, melting flat against the bark when noticed — its nature and intent are unknown.
Ashliel's repeated, increasingly pleading insistence that the party turn back south may conceal a reason she is not stating.
Ashliel has now explicitly forbidden the party from going north past the shrine stones, deepening the conflict with the checkpoint goal.
Ashliel now urges the party to take Sali and leave south at first light, widening the split between her wishes and the northward goal.
The party has crossed the shrine stones into the elves' wood against Ashliel's explicit warning — what consequence or pursuit follows from defying her is unresolved.
A tall barefoot woman in white with a wreath of yellow flowers watches the party from the edge of the city's light — her identity and intent are unknown.
Sali led the party north with a confidence and non-human humming she lacked at the chapel — why she knows this wood is unexplained.

The Lady of the Forest has confronted the party at the edge of the city's light and demands to know whether they seek something lost or mean to take what was never theirs — her judgment and intent are unresolved.
Sali claims she has dreamed of this place and knows the Lady — how she knows this wood and this goddess is unexplained.
A stag with a second pair of eyes inside its mouth stands motionless between two trunks just past the shrine stones — what it is and what it wants is unknown.
